direction.premise: Two contenders issue secret decrees that change how autonomous royals and neutral actors behave on a shared stone court.
direction.composition: The physical court is the visual center; a left-side bound ivory rule book keeps all five laws visible and a right-side illuminated document hand holds the real choices. On phone the board leads into five sigils and a horizontally swipeable hand.
direction.shapeLanguage: Asymmetric manuscript silhouettes, beveled stone, decorated parchment cuts and heraldic seals; full-height illustrated pieces stand on metal miniature bases.
direction.surfaceAndMaterial: Hand-authored local SVG illustrations supply faces, clothing, carved throne and medieval marginalia. Subtle warm paper, aged gold, steel, slate and wood-like carved edges separate functions.
direction.paletteLogic: Deep cobalt and oxblood distinguish contenders, original gold denotes the throne and crown progress, parchment backgrounds carry legible dark-ink laws, and neutral actors have individual costume hues.
direction.typography: Cormorant-style medieval serif headings with readable sans-serif rules and statuses, falling back to installed fonts offline.
direction.signature: Six distinct full-body court figures on a flat relief stage; legal slot panels look like a bound codex and player's hand like wax-signed illuminated decrees.
direction.distinction: The experience is a miniature living manuscript with a fixed 5x7 stage, not a neon dashboard, standard card catalog, full 3D board or static medieval wallpaper.

architecture.primaryVerb: Select an illustrated decree from your own hand, seal it, then read the combined law and shared board consequence.
architecture.physicalFeedback: A selected card is marked immediately; after both choices the round advances and the new public state persists.
architecture.spatialRationale: The shared royal board is followed by the current laws and a hand of selectable illustrated decree cards. This keeps the current game object and its real inputs spatially connected on a phone.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Blockies distributes pieces across an arcade play area; Crown Laws centers an immovable tall stone board within a legal ledger.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Blockies uses direct spatial actions on tiles; Crown Laws commits a private rule from a separate decree hand and watches actors resolve.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Cantica Glass organizes the experience as a linear framed stage with footer controls; Crown Laws pairs a long board with legislation.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Cantica Glass navigates sequential glasswork gestures, but Crown Laws seals simultaneous hidden commands before automatic resolution.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Moss & Marble is a landscape mini-golf course whose terrain and topology define the shot; Crown Laws is a fixed 5x7 court framed by an authoritative law book and a private decree hand.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Moss & Marble asks the player to aim and time a kinetic ball shot, while Crown Laws asks for one secret rule change and then resolves simultaneous autonomous actor movement.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Чепуха использует поочерёдное составление абсурдных высказываний на листах бумаги; Законы короны показывают постоянное игровое поле 5×7 с действующим кодексом слева и закрытой рукой общих указов справа.
comparisons.interactionDifference: В Чепухе игрок заполняет и передаёт бумажные ответы; здесь два скрытых закона разрешаются одновременно, после чего семь детерминированных фаз двигают автономных персонажей и награждают коронами.

production.renderer: DOM 5×7 board, native SVG vector path overlay, original manuscript actor atlas and a compact nine-stage parchment counsel panel. No new external textures or API services.
production.focalAsset: The same six royal miniatures gain semi-transparent counterfactual outlines and per-phase dotted trajectories, with a strong gold calligraphy-inspired panel.

motion.character: The selected scenario moves fully authored miniature silhouettes only to real deterministic engine coordinates; alternative ghost figures appear solely when the opposing conditional scenario differs.
motion.action: Switch current-law versus selected-decree scenarios without restarting the simulation. Phase keys expose actual moving actors and their routes.
motion.anticipation: Opening the advisor shifts focus to a compact parchment strip with nine selectable engine phases and an explicit conditional warning. The court stays fully readable.
motion.response: Each selected phase shows real log events, matching dotted movement trails and the actor positions recorded at that phase.
motion.followThrough: The last phase displays the full hypothetical outcome and visual differences, but the original turn, cards, player readiness and active PocketNet room remain unchanged.
motion.interruption: Any newer turn cancels the former timeline. Skip clears timer/effects and immediately displays the final authoritative result. Reduced-motion mode abbreviates every phase and suppresses moving VFX.
motion.reducedMotion: Animated route dashes and ghost breathing stop in reduced-motion mode; phase selector remains keyboard/touch accessible.

evidence.expectedChange: An autonomous board and a five-card hand appear
